s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of disorganized speech, anxiety, and self-harm behaviors with rapid progression of cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms
salient_findings: Abrupt onset of disorganized speech and self-harm behaviors
Rapid, fluent, and nonsensical speech
Development of agitation, persecutory delusions, and hallucinations
Urinary and fecal incontinence
Severe cognitive impairment with MMSE score of 2/30 and ACE-R score of 2/100
key_facts: 74-year-old right-handed woman
5-month history of symptoms
Symptoms began after a family trip
History of depression treated with sertraline
No prior cognitive impairment or neurological disease
Disoriented to time
Anomia and perseveration on Clock Drawing Test
Impaired performance on Luria’s three-step test
Defective crossed-pentagon drawing
Normal brain MRI 2 months after symptom onset
Initial diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease with no clinical improvement on memantine and quetiapine

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of disorganized speech, anxiety, and self-harm behaviors with prominent frontal and temporal features

shortlist.label: Primary progressive aphasia

shortlist.label: Dementia with Lewy bodies
shortlist.why_kept: Visual and auditory hallucinations, agitation, and fluctuating cognitive impairment

shortlist.label: Hashimoto's encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms, potentially treatable with immunotherapy
